author: agent-3
reviewStatus: AUTHORED SOLO. No second-party review. See threat-model.v1.json#reviewStatus.
purpose: Close the two remaining human-facing domains: distribution (how the thing arrives and is trusted) and authoring DX (how someone writes and debugs a rule).

decisionDependencies.claim: one installation may contain several signed artifacts; the promise is one install, not one file
TypeScript and Rust receive semantic providers
a provider invoking a real toolchain over untrusted source can execute repository code
network attacker on install or export
user-custody contracts need migrators; support windows are published
rules declare requirements; the planner materialises the least sufficient view

artifactSet.note: Contains the kernel, fact engine, declarative matcher, policy, and projections.
The portable floor. Must be present for every supported language or the capability tier is a lie.
Optional feature bundle. Absence degrades TypeScript to the syntax tier, reported as Coverage — not a broken install.
As above. Its substrate is P-4a and unresolved; its packaging consequences are therefore unknown.
Never required for any core path; absence is a typed unavailability.

installPromise.promise: One install command produces a working tool.
installPromise.notPromised: A single executable file. Optional providers and grammars may be separate signed assets.
installPromise.why: Promising one file would either force everything into the binary or make the promise false. The honest unit is the installation.

tiers.meaning: CI-verified every release; a failure blocks the release
Builds and smoke-tests; failures are bugs, not release blockers

platformMatrix.rule: A platform's tier is published. An unlisted platform is unsupported by default, never implicitly supported.
platformMatrix.note: Which OS/arch belongs in which tier is a product decision this artifact does not make.

rules: Every shipped artifact is signed, including optional provider bundles. An unsigned optional bundle is the easiest supply-chain entry point (TM.ADV4).
The host verifies signature and version compatibility BEFORE executing any provider or adapter — at admission, not at first use.
Contribution bundles carry a digest recorded in the lockfile; the digest enters PlanId, so a substituted bundle changes analysis identity rather than silently changing results.
A build should be reproducible enough that an independent rebuild yields matching digests. Recorded as a goal, not claimed as achieved.
Signing raises the cost of substitution. It does not defend against a malicious first-party release — that is threat-model non-goal N5.

airGap.requirement: Full analysis capability with no network, at any time, including first run.
implications: An offline bundle contains host, grammars, and selected providers with all transitive assets — no fetch-on-first-use of grammars or toolchains.
Nothing may be resolved lazily from a network on the analysis path. A lazily-fetched grammar makes the product silently online.

Migrators must ship IN the release. An air-gapped user who skipped releases cannot fetch a migrator, so a user-custody migration that requires download is unreachable for them — this is a real interaction between the air-gap requirement and the versioning policy that the versioning artifact flagged and did not solve.
Update checks are opt-in and never on the analysis path.

updatePosture.decision: No self-mutating updater in the core.
updatePosture.why: A tool whose job is deterministic evidence should not rewrite its own binary. It breaks the version-to-evidence binding and adds an unnecessary privileged code path.
updatePosture.allowed: Reporting that a newer version exists, opt-in, off the analysis path.

authoringDX.principle: A rule author's loop must not require publishing anything, and the tool must be able to explain why a rule did not fire. Both are correctness features, not conveniences: an author who cannot see why a rule was silent will write a rule that is silently wrong.

requirements: A local path or lockfile override loads a contribution from disk with no registry involvement.
The local loop uses the SAME admission, capability, and validation path as a published bundle. A rule that works locally and fails on install means the local loop was a different code path.
First-party rules dogfood the identical authoring surface. If they use a private path, the public one is untested.

explainability.requirement: `explain` answers 'why did this rule not fire here?' with a typed trace, not prose.
traceContents: the Coverage entries it consumed, with the compound key
candidate subjects considered and the count excluded at each filter
whether it was evaluated, skipped-requirements-unmet, budget-exceeded, or faulted
for skipped: the exact unmet requirement, including a language capability tier where that is the reason (P-4 loud tiering)
explainability.why: Under predicate-relative sufficiency a rule may legitimately not run. Without an explanation that is indistinguishable from a rule that ran and found nothing — and those two have opposite meanings.

factExploration.requirement: A bounded, typed query surface over a stored fact view, usable without authoring a rule.
factExploration.constraint: It is the same typed query API surfaced elsewhere; it never runs analysis or creates a Run, and returns typed unavailable when facts are missing.
factExploration.why: An author who cannot inspect facts writes rules against an imagined schema.

testKit.requirement: Fixture-based rule tests with recorded expected verdicts, runnable locally, identical to the release gate G2.
testKit.rule: A rule contribution without fixtures is admissible but is reported as unverified. Calibration is the asset; a rule with no fixtures has none.

conformanceTests.assert: With no network available at any point, including first run, a full analysis completes on a supported language.
Absence of an optional semantic provider degrades the affected language to the syntax tier with typed Coverage, and does not fail the install or the run.
An unsigned or digest-mismatched provider or contribution is refused at admission, before execution.
Substituting a contribution bundle changes PlanId.
No grammar, toolchain, or migrator is fetched from a network on the analysis path.
An unlisted platform reports unsupported rather than attempting and failing obscurely.
A contribution loaded by local path traverses the same admission and capability checks as a published one.
`explain` on a rule that did not fire distinguishes skipped-requirements-unmet from evaluated-with-no-findings, and names the unmet requirement.
`explain` names the language capability tier as the reason where that is the reason (P-4).
The fact-exploration surface creates no Run and returns typed unavailable for missing relations.
A rule contribution without fixtures is admitted and reported as unverified.
A provider that can execute repository-controlled code is refused unless explicitly granted, and the grant is visible in PlanId (TM.F1).

sealedPropertiesCovered.property: the language capability tier is honest and observable
compatibility is negotiated at admission, not at first use
execution-capable resolution requires an explicit grant (TM.F1)
first-party dogfoods the public authoring surface
a silent rule is distinguishable from a satisfied rule

peerReviewRequired: The air-gap/migrator interaction is identified but unsolved: an offline user who skipped releases cannot fetch a migrator, and shipping every historical migrator in every release is unbounded. This needs a real answer.
Is 'no self-mutating updater' right for a CLI whose users expect one? It is defensible on evidence-binding grounds but is a UX cost.
Should a fixture-less rule be admissible at all, versus refused? This artifact chose admitted-but-unverified.
knownLimitations: No concrete platform assignments — the tier structure is defined, the contents are a product decision.
Rust provider packaging is unknowable until P-4a resolves the substrate, so its size, licensing, and air-gap implications are unstated.
Reproducible builds are a stated goal with no mechanism.
The air-gap/migrator conflict is recorded as unsolved, not solved.
